decisions.answer: Advisory plus apply for low-risk decision points; every acceptance, security, and completion gate stays deterministic.
decisions.question: How much authority may Jev's typed decisions have?
decisions.rationale: User wants deep exploitation without delegating any gate; the calibration found no validated auto-accept gate.

decisions.answer: Non-safety internals (spike candidacy, deep-research dispatch, ready-set ordering, add-only review assignment, secret pre-flag, conditional-skill rankings), guarded routing, and add-only review influence.
decisions.question: Which decision points may apply (change behavior)?
decisions.rationale: Every applied point is reversible and non-authoritative; guarded routing acts only when the deterministic router found no route or Jev agrees.

decisions.answer: request/2 decision field, --use-jev flag, and a natural-language phrase; only the field and flag activate code, the NL phrase is instruction-led.
decisions.question: How does the user initiate Jev for a run?
decisions.rationale: Machine surfaces stay auditable; the NL phrase is translated by the host operator, never parsed by code.

decisions.answer: A single global switch; enabling Jev runs the apply set plus all advisory points.
decisions.question: What is the granularity of opt-in?
decisions.rationale: User chose maximum exploitation and simple operation over per-point control.

decisions.answer: A declared host-mediated capability in capabilities/3; the transport lives in the driver/host and is injected like the executor; skills never perform the fetch.
decisions.question: How is the live Jev call authorized given disabled network/credentials postures?
decisions.rationale: Preserves the fail-closed injected-executor doctrine and keeps egress auditable.

decisions.answer: Tracked .agents/decisions/ artifacts, with a new agents-index class and a ## decisions/ README section.

decisions.rationale: Durable audit of applied decisions; requires the section-anchored index writer.

decisions.answer: Jev-enabled runs may use the main checkout; the decision writer uses section-anchored inserts and check-suite/hygiene are run after.
decisions.question: Where do Jev-enabled runs execute?
decisions.rationale: User chose convenience; foreign untracked artifacts are never staged and only owned paths are written.

decisions.answer: Per-call caps only (timeout, max state bytes, max cost per call); there is no run-level budget.
decisions.question: What budget bounds a Jev-enabled run?
decisions.rationale: User chose simplicity; measured ~$0.000021/call makes dollars negligible, so the real bound is per-call and per-point call count.

decisions.answer: Keep OPENROUTER_ROUTER_KEY as-is with no rotation; it is read host-side only, never on argv or in artifacts.
decisions.question: How is the Jev/OpenRouter key handled and rotated?
decisions.rationale: User accepted the residual exposure risk; transport reads the key from the environment only.

decisions.answer: Whenever Jev is enabled and returns an answer; there is no confidence gate, with fallback only on transport failure or low agreement with a deterministic baseline.
decisions.question: When may an apply-set decision change behavior?
decisions.rationale: User chose maximal exploitation; deterministic-baseline agreement and reversibility remain the guardrails.

decisions.answer: No calibration is required; decisions are logged with baseline agreement and a kill switch remains available.
decisions.question: Does enabling apply require calibration first?
decisions.rationale: User chose speed over validation; the finding's calibration caveats are recorded as residual risk, not a gate.

decisions.answer: The apply set runs with behavior effect and all remaining advisory points run as recorded advice.
decisions.question: Under the global switch, what does 'all points' mean?
decisions.rationale: Matches the literal global-switch choice and maximizes observability.

decisions.answer: Only the explicit-mode skills are denied; Jev may route any conditional skill, including csm-review.
decisions.question: Which skills must Jev never be the sole router for?
decisions.rationale: User chose the narrower denylist; the deterministic router still owns every route it can resolve.

ideaStatement: Add an optional, user-initiated Jev (TypeSafe) typed-decision layer to the CSM skills: off by default, enabled by a global switch via a request/2 decision field, a --use-jev flag, or a natural-language phrase; non-safety decision points may apply (guarded routing, add-only review, reversible internals) while every acceptance, security, and completion gate stays deterministic; all other points are recorded advice; the host-mediated transport fails open to the skill's existing harness model when Jev is unreachable or out of credit.

researchSynthesis: The layer is grounded in a three-stage research program: Jev deep research, an ability-to-skill mapping, and a change design, then an independent adversarial challenge, a live 20-call experiment, a 195-item 227-call calibration, and an independent verification. Live-verified: POST https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with OPENROUTER_ROUTER_KEY returns typed decisions for typesafe/jev-1.13 (~$0.0000211/call, median 329ms, output free); the choice space is the criteria record's keys (criteria is required); the native api.typesafe.ai endpoint rejects this key; the chat endpoint rejects the model. The skills currently use subagent LLM fan-out for generation and deterministic code for most typed decisions; csm-orchestrate has no model runtime and an explicitly injected executor, so the adapter is injected the same way. Calibration reached 94.9% on a synthetic rule-labelled corpus but found no validated auto-accept gate: five of six derived thresholds are 'accept everything', the one structured point still auto-accepts its confident errors (privacy->security 0.94, data-integrity->destructive 0.86), confidence is not the argmax probability in 106/195 cases, and no human-labelled held-out set exists; injection was resisted 0/8 and repeats were byte-stable. The SCOUT corrected four finding errors: csm-plan already declares broker/host-mediated egress (only csm-build and csm-review are disabled/none); routing spans two seams (run-orchestrator.mjs:437 and phase-compiler.mjs:169-206); the adapter must live under csm-orchestrate/lib/** because root lib/ is not packed; and capabilities/3 plus request/2 are unavoidable because the schemas are additionalProperties:false. The DEEP_DIVE confirmed the design is integrable without touching any gate, provided three constraints hold: the adapter stays in the packed skill tree, decision data never enters the per-node request or receipt (materialDigest strips only status/requestDigest), and opt-in uses a real request/2 rather than an added field. The dominant residual risk is call-count and latency blow-up inside retry/remediation/review loops, boundable with per-point call caps, single-flight and in-run result caching, a run-scoped circuit breaker, and a kill switch; the dominant correctness risk is applying a confidently-wrong adjacent-taxonomy classification, mitigated by restricting applies to reversible non-authoritative points, add-only review, deterministic-baseline agreement, and an audit artifact per applied decision. Fail-open behavior is specified: out-of-credit (402), uncontactable (network/timeout/5xx), rate-limited (429), auth/permission (401/403), and model/config errors all revert to the harness model or deterministic baseline, record a skipped decision, and never pause the skill; Jev quota is distinct from the main-model Pause On Quota.
